merger_name: Respect Group – Clifton Co-op Hospital aged care, support at home care and community housing, Clifton QLD
merger_description:
Respect Group Limited (**Respect Group**) proposes to acquire 100% of the business, land and assets of Clifton Co-op Hospital Ltd (**CCH**) (the **Acquisition**).

Respect Group is a not-for-profit registered charity and unlisted public company based in Tasmania, which provides residential aged care, retirement living and support at home services. Respect Group owns and operates 47 residential aged care homes across Tasmania, New South Wales, Victoria, Western Australia, Queensland and South Australia. Respect Group operates support at home services in Tasmania, Western Australia, New South Wales and Victoria.

CCH is a member-owned co-operative based in Clifton, Queensland, governed by the Co-operatives National Law. CCH operates a residential aged care and provides support at home services and community housing services, in Clifton, Queensland.

Each of the parties provides funded residential care services and support at home in accordance with the *Aged Care Act 2024* (Cth), although Respect Group does not provide support at home services in Queensland. CCH also provides community housing in Queensland.

Following completion of the Acquisition, Respect Group will continue to operate the services previously provided by CCH.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no geographic overlap between Respect Group and
CCH in the supply of support at home services in
Queensland
b. there is limited geographic overlap between Respect Group
and CCH in the supply of residential age care services, with
Respect Groups closest existing facilities being located over
74 kilometres away by road
c. there are alternative providers of residential age care
services in the region surrounding CCH.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
